<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/api.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**42** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63b86b385dd2cbfeba131438112c49be2c74df91`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/api.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/data/:object (route, 76 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63b86b385dd2cbfeba131438112c49be2c74df91` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9ed311cb85d83c624ec815e936a829b9426fbc65` — the merge of head `8738359bde443b9bca880039ffb1b5d017d61813` into base `63b86b385dd2cbfeba131438112c49be2c74df91`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9ed311cb85d83c624ec815e936a829b9426fbc65 && git checkout 9ed311cb85d83c624ec815e936a829b9426fbc65
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 63b86b385dd2cbfeba131438112c49be2c74df91 8738359bde443b9bca880039ffb1b5d017d61813 && git checkout -B drift-repro 63b86b385dd2cbfeba131438112c49be2c74df91 && git merge --no-ff 8738359bde443b9bca880039ffb1b5d017d61813

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63b86b385dd2cbfeba131438112c49be2c74df91
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 63b86b385dd2cbfeba131438112c49be2c74df91` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bc7630ee57def483853be294b43e2771238ec002`
Local-runs: none
Scope: card #29896 and its comments (6601906029, 6623292940, 6624449982); the seat order and `/mnt/project-files/issue-29896/os-dev-report.json`; the PR body, files, full diff and the head's check-runs. At `pr-30021`: `packages/spec/src/api/sortability.zod.ts` and its test; `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts` (`resolveQueryFields`, `assertSortFieldsExist`, `assertSortFieldsAreOffered`, `UNMATERIALIZED_SORT_TYPES`); `protocol.ts` (`findData` and the sort docblock); `packages/rest/src/data-sort-field-sortable-flag-door.test.ts`, `crud-routes.ts`, `data-action-routes.ts` (export), `record-page-routes.ts`; `packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts`, `mcp.ts`; `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`, `mcp-http-tools.ts`, `plugin.ts`; `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (`assertOrderByIsMaterializable`), `registry.ts` (`mergeObjectDefinitions`); `packages/spec/src/data/field-customization.ts`, `authorable-surface.base.json`, `liveness/field.json`, `api-surface/api.json`, `export-origins/api.json`; the semantic entries `17.engine-find-formula-order-by-refused.ts` and `17.sort-node-direction-rejected.ts`; `packages/lint/src/validate-sortable-fields.ts`; the changeset. Cited ui code read, not reviewed: `plugin-grid` `objectGridGenerateColumns.tsx`, `ObjectGrid.tsx`; `plugin-list` `ListView.tsx`; `core` `column-sortability.ts`. On main: AGENTS.md step 3, `contract-review.md`, `SKILL.md:313`, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, ADR-0087.

Face: accept-set narrowing at the Data API list door (`GET /api/v1/data/:object?sort=`, `POST /data/:object/query`, export, RPC). A sort that names a field whose author declared `sortable: false` used to answer `200` sorted and now answers `400 INVALID_SORT`. There is also a published-schema move: the `FieldSortabilitySchema.reason` enum widens and `FIELD_UNSORTABLE_AUTHOR_DECLARED` is a new export. Run in-seat as an isolated reviewer at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, fed the card, the PR and the head's check-runs only.

### ① Derived judgments
- **The projection change is correct.** `resolveObjectSortability` reads only a literal `false`, and only after the virtual check. No key, `true`, `0` or `null` all project `sortable: true`, while a `formula` with `sortable: false` projects `virtual-type`, so the door and the projection agree. Both array and map field shapes are read. The unprovisioned-anchor loop cannot overwrite an author's `false`. System columns are absent from the projection, so they stay accepted. An extender cannot patch `sortable` onto an owner's field: `mergeObjectDefinitions` replaces a field whole, and the whitelist excludes `sortable`. The door and the projection read the same merged registry object.
- **The door refusal is correct on every `findData` path, but one public door is still open.** `assertSortFieldsAreOffered` is the fourth verdict, after unknown, dotted and unmaterializable, and it uses the same `invalidSortError`. Every `findData` caller reaches it: REST list, query, export, record-page `related[].sort`, RPC, and the runtime MCP domain. **The stdio MCP `query_records` does not.** `stdio-data-bridge.ts` `query()` forwards `orderBy` straight into `engine.find` (L993–999, wired by `plugin.ts:727`), and the engine door judges `formula` only. That call still answers sorted by a `sortable: false` field. "Every caller of `findData` passes this door" is true but not sufficient. Category 6 now says the key governs "the Data API", and the changeset's **Not changed** names only hooks and flows.
- **A stored view's sort is now refused at read time, and the changeset misstates it.** `ListViewSchema.sort` is authored metadata. `ListView.tsx` seeds `currentSort` from `schema.sort` and sends it to the server unfiltered (L3186). `filterPlatformSortableSort` applies only to the header and to the emit/persist path. Lint `validate-sortable-fields` judges only the virtual predicate. So a published view whose `sort` names a `sortable: false` field used to load sorted, and after this PR every fetch of it answers 400, with no authoring gate between. The sentence "A sort the door now refuses is a request, never a stored value" is false.
- **The Clause-② line is right.** `yes (narrowing)` is well-formed and the arm is correct.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` is wrong, on two grounds.**
  - (a) `authorable-surface.base.json` lists `api/FieldSortability:reason`. A new accepted enum member is therefore at least `added`. A green `check:authorable-surface` does not settle this, because that gate tracks keys, not enum members.
  - (b) An authored view `sort` is now refused, which makes it `narrowed`, as the seat order anticipated.

  The kind is `narrowed`, so at least `minor` is owed on the moved packages, and both `patch` entries are wrong.
- **The ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is wrong.** A stored surface moves (a view's `sort`), and the body prescribes a remedy ("drops the sort … removes `sortable: false`"). The precedent is exact: `17.engine-find-formula-order-by-refused` registered an entry for an ORDER BY refusal with one author-reachable stored surface.
- **Liveness is right.** `sortable` stays `live` and gains evidence and a note.
- **The ui half, read only, is half right.** Under `manualSortingOn`, `withSortability` overrides the explicit column's `sortable`, so the header is correct there. The ListView Sort picker reads the projection. Client-side sorting still offers the header, and the fetch does not filter the stored sort, so a `domain:ui` card is owed.
- **The pins and the ablation are adequate for the order's scope.** The real `GET` route runs with zero driver reads, the four sort shapes are pinned, and the controls cover no key, `true` and formula. One ablation turns the door pin red. Not pinned: the stdio MCP door, the engine path (the **Not changed** claim is asserted, not measured), and a stored view sort through the Console.

### ② Semver level
Declared: `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, the BREAKING banner, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Judged: Clause-② is right, and `Metadata-protocol` is `narrowed`. Each moved package therefore takes `minor`, and the ADR-0087 disposition becomes `registered <id>` with a semantic entry. `check-changeset-no-major` passed only because `none` + `patch` agree with each other; the kind itself is wrong. The changeset is not consistent with the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags
- Stdio MCP `query_records` still sorts by a `sortable: false` field (REWORK-3).
- Authoring gap: lint `validate-sortable-fields` does not judge a view `sort` that names a `sortable: false` field. The seat files this card, and the semantic entry names it as the remedy's gate.
- A `domain:ui` card is owed: ListView's fetch-side sort filter (L3186), and the header under client-side sorting. The seat files it.
- Record page `related[].sort` is now refused per part through `findData`. If the Console builds it from authored related-list metadata, that is a second stored surface. The dev verifies this and names it in the entry.
- Check-runs at review: lint, typecheck, liveness and the PR-body guards green; the Core, UI and E2E suites still in progress.

### ④ Narrowing face
- `sortability.zod.ts`: the resolver is correct. The category-6 docblock's claim that the key governs "the Data API" is false for stdio `query_records`.
- `protocol-query-validation.ts`: the placement, the error constructor and the "ingress only" docblock are all correct. What is wrong is the declaration around the code, not the code itself.
- Changeset changes owed:
  - `Metadata-protocol: none` → `narrowed`.
  - Every moved package → `minor`.
  - The ADR-0087 disposition → `registered <id>`.
  - Strike "never a stored value".
  - **Not changed** names the stdio door, unless the PR closes it.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-kqbqmk`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzibcN9oHa8kDbTTnL5`

**VERDICT: REWORK**

REWORK items:
1. **(blocking)** Set `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` in both the PR body and the changeset, and raise `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` to `minor`. Then re-run `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration` against the new body.
2. **(blocking)** Change the ADR-0087 disposition to `registered <id>`. Add a semantic entry under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/` on the precedent `17.engine-find-formula-order-by-refused.ts`:
   - Surface: a list view `sort` that names a `sortable: false` field, plus the record-page `related[].sort` if it is authored.
   - Replacement: drop the sort, or remove `sortable: false`.
   - Acceptance: no view `sort` names such a field.

   Regenerate the registry, and strike "A sort the door now refuses is a request, never a stored value".
3. **(blocking)** The stdio MCP door (`stdio-data-bridge.ts` `query` → `engine.find`) needs one of two fixes:
   - Refuse there with the same `INVALID_SORT` and pin it. This is preferred, because it is the same projection in the same package's bridge.
   - Or state in **Not changed** and in the category-6 docblock that stdio `query_records` still sorts by the field, and report it back so the seat files the card.
4. (seat) File the lint card for `validate-sortable-fields` and the `domain:ui` card for ListView's fetch filter and the client-side-sorting header.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8738359bde443b9bca880039ffb1b5d017d61813`
Local-runs: none
Scope: the REWORK record 6624674350 in full; `git diff bc7630ee..8738359b` (three linear commits, 7 files, +225/−18); the head's check-runs and the failing Check Changeset job log; the replacement body `/mnt/project-files/issue-29896/pr-body-r1.md` against the live body.

At `8738359b`:
- the changeset;
- `18.field-sortable-false-sort-refused.ts`, against `SemanticMigration`, the precedent `17.engine-find-formula-order-by-refused.ts`, `semantic-relevance.test.ts`, the registry and upgrade-guide builders, and `.gitignore`;
- `stdio-data-bridge.ts` (`unofferedSortRefusal`, `query()`, `stdioObjectView`, `enforceApiExposure`), its new test, and `mcp-http-tools.ts` (the `sort → orderBy` alias, tool-error rendering);
- `protocol-query-validation.ts`, `invalidSortError`, `assertOrderByIsMaterializable`, `sortability.zod.ts`, `liveness/field.json`.

The stored surfaces:
- `RecordRelatedListProps.sort`, `ElementDataSourceSchema.sort` and `PageComponentSchema.dataSource`;
- `recordPageRelatedLists`, `record-page-routes.ts` (`orderBy: entry.sort` → `findData`), `record-related-list.tsx`, `RelatedList.tsx`, `ListView.tsx`;
- `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: what each reads, and from where.

Face: delta review of the fix-up after REWORK 6624674350. The round-2 change is confined to the declaration, one new semantic entry, the stdio MCP door with its three-test pin, the category-6 docblock with its regenerated page, and the liveness note. `protocol-query-validation.ts`, `protocol.ts`, `engine.ts`, the rest pin and the resolver are byte-identical to round 1.

### ① Derived judgments
- **REWORK-1 is closed in the changeset.**
  - Declaration: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and the newly moved `@objectstack/mcp` are all `minor`. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` has one arm.
  - The head's ADR-0087 gate reads `registered field-sortable-false-sort-refused (new here)`.
  - The one red, `check-changeset-no-major`, fails only because it reads `Metadata-protocol: none` from the **live PR body**. The replacement body says `narrowed`, so this red is the seat's apply step, not the diff.
- **REWORK-2 is closed.**
  - Entry: it carries every required `SemanticMigration` field and no `conversionIds` / `relevantWhen`, so the relevance roster is untouched, and the spec suite is green.
  - Registry: `registry.ts` is gitignored and generated at install and build, and the upgrade guide is generated too. `check:spec-changes` and `check:upgrade-guide` are green.
  - The id is new in the diff. "Never a stored value" is struck and replaced by a **Stored sorts** bullet.
- **Every listed stored surface is real and reaches the door.**
  - `RecordRelatedListProps.sort` is copied into `related[].sort`, and `record-page-routes.ts` passes it as `orderBy` into `findData`. The list's own read also sends it as `$orderby`.
  - The related list's `dataSource.sort` maps onto `defaultSort` and is sent the same way.
  - The list view `sort` was established in round 1.
- **The surface list is under-inclusive, but not wrong.** The entry names only the related list's `dataSource.sort`, yet more stored sorts reach the same door:
  - every page element's `ElementDataSourceSchema.sort`: list-view block, kanban, map, gantt, timeline, report;
  - a list page's own `sort` (`page.zod.ts:1057`);
  - an app page `record` binding's `sort` (`:878`).

  The acceptance criteria ("grep your views and pages for each sort field") cover them in substance. Filed.
- **REWORK-3 is closed by the preferred fix, and it judges by the same projection.**
  - Placement: `unofferedSortRefusal` runs after the exposure gate and the stored-metadata refusals, and before `engine.find`.
  - Verdict: it calls the same `resolveObjectSortability(def).fields` with the data door's predicate. The object comes from the protocol's merged object listing, which is the same merged registry object the data door reads. So the two doors cannot disagree on a verdict.
- **The error shape is the Data API's, with one truthful difference.**
  - Same stamps: `INVALID_SORT`, `status: 400`, `field`, `fields`, `object`. `httpStatus: 400` is added, as the engine's own `INVALID_SORT` does.
  - The difference: `param: 'orderBy'`, which is the tool's real argument name.
  - Message: the same clause and remedy, plus "the query was not run". It is rendered as a tool error, and that is pinned.
- **Precedence differs in one benign respect.** For an `orderBy` that names both a formula field and a `sortable: false` field, REST names the formula first and stdio names the `sortable: false` field first. Both answer `400 INVALID_SORT`. The docblock's "fourth verdict" is true of the verdict's identity, not of its position on this transport. An unknown `orderBy` on stdio still reaches the driver, which is pre-existing and not moved here.
- **The HTTP MCP path is unchanged** and goes through `findData`, closed in round 1.
- **Pins and ablation.**
  - Three tests: the refusal alone and behind a sortable field, with `engine.find` never called; the controls (no key, `true`, no sort, a filter on the field) reach the engine; and the rendered envelope.
  - Reported, not re-run here: before/after 2 failed | 1 passed → 3 passed, and one ablation that turns the two refusal tests red.
  - `sortable` stays `live`, and its note names the new pin.

### ② Semver level
`minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/mcp`. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, BREAKING, `<!-- adr-0087: registered field-sortable-false-sort-refused -->`. Judged the same.
- Kind: `narrowed`, because a stored view `sort` and a `record:related_list` `sort` are refused at read. The new refusal at the public stdio tool is a second arm of the same kind, and it is declared in the Clause-② line, the banner, Before/Now and the entry.
- Consistency: the changeset agrees with the diff. The live body does not, and the replacement does.

### ③ Boundary flags
- Check Changeset stays red until the seat applies `pr-body-r1.md`. Everything else at the head is green: Test Core 8/8, Test UI 16/16, Type Check including test-typecheck, Lint & Repo Gates, liveness, Dogfood and the PR-body guards.
- The entry under-lists the stored surfaces (see ①). This is filed with the lint card #30023's scope.
- The stdio docblock's "fourth sort verdict" can take a one-sentence note on a later touch. It is not owed here.

### ④ Narrowing face
- `stdio-data-bridge.ts`: the placement, the shared resolver, the envelope and the message are correct. `unofferedSortRefusal` is package-internal, and `index.ts` does not publish it.
- `18.field-sortable-false-sort-refused.ts`: the shape, the precedent and the remedy are right. The surface prose widens on a follow-up.
- The changeset and `pr-body-r1.md` are consistent:
  - Clause-② has one arm, and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`.
  - `Skills-docs: none — REASON` is in the closed vocabulary, and the marker resolves.
  - **Not changed** no longer needs the stdio door.

## 席位核对

Verdict: **ACCEPT** at head `8738359bde443b9bca880039ffb1b5d017d61813` · 2026-11-04T08:04Z

- **Shape:** the sortability projection honours an authored `field.sortable: false` with the new reason `author-declared`. The data door (`findData`: REST list, query, export, record-page related reads, RPC, runtime MCP) and the stdio MCP `query_records` refuse such a sort `400 INVALID_SORT`. The PR adds one ADR-0087 semantic entry and minor changesets.
- **Reviews:** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review 6624674350 was REWORK, with three items. The delta review at this head is PASS.
- **Premise measured:** the filer's 4/4 reproduction was re-measured on main. The real `GET /data/:object` route refuses it with zero driver reads, and the stdio door refuses before `engine.find`. Ablations: the projection branch, and the stdio throw made unreachable, each red, then restored.
- **Declaration:**
  - `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`.
  - Minor on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/mcp`.
  - BREAKING, with `adr-0087: registered field-sortable-false-sort-refused`.

  Reviewed as correct.
- **Gates (head):** mcp 663, spec 24376, rest pin 6/6, eslint 0, the changeset gate and the ADR-0087 gate exit 0 with the revised body, 107 dispatch-gates exit 0, and dogfood 416 files / 3456 tests. In CI, only Check Changeset is red, because it reads the stale live body.
- **Accepted deviations:**
  - The harness-pinned branch `claude/project-thread-kqbqmk`.
  - The engine door is left unchanged, so hooks and flows still sort freely, as **Not changed** states.
  - Out of scope and filed: #30023 (lint judges stored sorts; it also takes the wider page `dataSource.sort` surfaces) and #30024 (the ui fetch-side filter).
  - The seat applies the signed trailer and the replacement body through the relay.
- **Landing:** on all-green at this head, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay. The protocol.ts codemod window (#29985) opens after this merges.
